jobs.prompt:
truthful popup and requester action states

Implement truthful popup and requester action states. In the popup and capture panel, start in a neutral checking state until authoritative status arrives. Make a failed status check visibly retryable. Hide requester Start during active work and keep Cancel accessible; restore Start only when normal spend, setup and context guards pass. Render a pending marketplace Stop as progress, keeping Start unavailable until authoritative settlement, and retain real errors. Use the existing mode-aware URL policy for the configured loopback fixture tab only. Surface linked-account tab-open failures in visible recovery UI, keeping the action retryable. On reopen, reconcile a timed-out Start against authoritative worker state and retain a retryable unknown when inconclusive. Preserve duplicate-click locking and explicit signed-out setup. Verify through the normal entry points. #15: Delay active and inactive status responses and reject a third; assert initial action visibility and the final action or visible retry. #66: Drive active, cancelled and settled requester states and check Cancel and guarded Start. #67: Compare pending, failed and completed Stop, including disabled state and diagnostic visibility. #69: Assert one Start for the allowed fixture route, and local, HTTP, foreign or unsupported routes remain rejected in production; check wrong-tab recovery and duplicate clicks. #71: Reject open for a linked account, retry successfully, and cover signed-out setup. #124: Advance past the popup deadline, apply the late enabled state, reopen and assert no failed receipt. Work in the extension source and its local tests. Use generated DOM fixtures, mocked browser/storage/transport APIs and fake clocks as appropriate. Keep verification offline and use fictional records. Do not contact any live service, use credentials or customer data, or operate a real account. Inspect current implementation before editing. Report the changed files, commands actually run, per-issue assertions and any unverified acceptance criteria.

Target issues: #15, #66, #67, #69, #71, #124. Lead this issue group as gpt-6.2-astra at ultra effort. Use gpt-6.2-sol developers at max effort with separate file ownership and independent verification. Use the repository's normal local checks and generated synthetic fixtures. First inspect the current code and tests; when the base already satisfies an item, establish that directly. Retain existing fixes. For each numbered issue report its concrete behavior, tracked regression coverage and the exact commands and outcomes. Run the repository's complete affected test suites and update generated content hashes where required. Do not deploy, use production systems, change external settings or publish sensitive data. Finish on your result branch.

Fix dashboard interaction ordering using the normal UI entry points

Fix dashboard interaction ordering using the normal UI entry points. With an in-memory extension adapter, confirm a vocabulary refresh dispatches its discovery operation once, and settles on success and on an explicit error. Use controlled promises to finish cached rows and reset selection while a same-scope balance read is pending. The balance should still appear, equivalent balance reads should coalesce, and stale export estimates should be discarded. Navigate and type in a different form during workspace bootstrap, then release verification and assert the same input and value survive. For a first billing visit, paint the shell immediately but read the first ledger page after an expiring test grant has been reconciled and committed. Verify the initial page includes its expiration entry, paging still works, and a failed refresh can recover. Use offline browser and store fixtures, no real accounts or extensions.
